Keywords: Henry III Liege Homage to Louis IX
RagShortTexts: In December 1259, Henry III performed liege homage to Saint Louis IX, sealing the Treaty of Paris.

Variants.Content: On 4 December 1259, King Henry III of England did liege homage to King Louis IX of France in Paris, ratifying the Treaty of Paris. Henry gave up his ancestral claims to Normandy, Anjou, Maine, and Poitou, which had been lost to the Capetians earlier in the century, and he held Gascony as a peer of France. The settlement brought an uneasy peace between the two crowns. Henry's homage bound him to Louis as a vassal for his continental lands, and both courts understood that the peace would last only as long as the terms held.

English barons chafed at the sight of their sovereign kneeling before the French king, and every magnate asked what the homage cost the realm. A Gascon lord who swore fealty to the English crown now served two masters, and he had to weigh each demand from Paris against the royal writs from London.
With royal seals affixed in Paris, vineyard workers along the Garonne find respite from pillaging. English wool convoys move through French fair towns without fear of border arrest.
